finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST /hooks/test makes a server-side HTTP POST to a caller-supplied URL (req.body.callback) with no allowlist, scheme check, or IP/host restriction. Redirects are followed by default and the upstream status code is returned to the caller. Severity HIGH if the pub router is publicly reachable; downgrade to MEDIUM if pub is mounted behind authentication outside this repo.
finding.source: req.body.callback (routes.js:20), attacker-controlled request body on the unauthenticated pub router (routes.js:19)
finding.sink: axios.post(req.body.callback, { ping: true }) (routes.js:20); status returned at routes.js:21

trace.note: pub router defined with no auth middleware; only admin.use(requireAdmin) is attached to the admin router (line 12)
req.body.callback read directly and passed as the URL to axios.post
res.json returns r.status to the caller, giving a port-scan and reachability oracle

finding.guards_checked: No scheme restriction, hostname allowlist, URL parsing, private/link-local/loopback IP blocking, or redirect-disable (axios follows redirects by default) anywhere in the path. requireAdmin (routes.js:7-10) is not applied to pub. The only check is that req.body exists, which is not a security control. Open question: the mount point of pub and whether it sits behind auth or a webhook-purpose exemption cannot be verified from this repo.

verdict.guard_found: none. routes.js:7-10 (requireAdmin) is attached only to the admin router at routes.js:12, and no URL validation, host allowlist, IP blocking, or redirect restriction exists between routes.js:19 and routes.js:21.
verdict.reason: Every trace line checks out (routes.js:4, 12, 19-21 match the claim), and no closing guard exists on the path, but whether the unauthenticated pub router at routes.js:4 is reachable by a remote attacker depends on how it is mounted, and the only file in this directory is routes.js, so the source's attacker-controllability cannot be confirmed.

finding.claim: Admin-only GET /diagnostics/fetch makes a server-side GET to a caller-supplied URL (req.query.url) with no allowlist, scheme check, or IP restriction. Redirects are followed and the upstream status code is returned. Severity MEDIUM because the caller must hold an admin session, which the skill does not treat as closing SSRF to metadata or RFC-1918 targets.
finding.source: req.query.url (routes.js:15), attacker-controlled query string on an admin route

trace.note: admin.use(requireAdmin) applies the session role check to every admin route
requireAdmin only checks req.session.role === 'admin'; this is an authorization gate, not an URL allowlist
req.query.url passed directly to axios.get with no validation
res.json returns r.status to the caller

finding.guards_checked: Admin session check (routes.js:7-12) only. No hostname allowlist, scheme restriction, or IP-range blocking, and redirects are followed by default. The admin-role-equals-server-access exception does not apply because nothing in the code shows the admin role grants OS-level access. Also not handled: req.query.url may be an array, which axios would reject, so it is not a bypass.

verdict.guard_found: none (no URL allowlist, scheme check, or IP restriction). The only check is the admin role gate at routes.js:8, applied via routes.js:12 and reached at routes.js:14.
verdict.reason: The trace lines are accurate (routes.js:8, 12, 14, 15, 16), but the source fails the controllability check: req.query.url at routes.js:15 is only reachable after requireAdmin (routes.js:8) passes, so the value is supplied by an admin session rather than by an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker, which the rubric requires for CONFIRMED. The missing URL restriction is a hardening gap for an admin-only route, not a finding under the stated criteria.
